issues.sym: You have to add oil between changes, sometimes as much as a quart every few hundred miles. There may be no low-oil warning until the engine runs short, then misfires, stalling or loss of power.
issues.why: The piston rings on this 2.4L engine can let oil into the cylinders, and a clogged PCV (crankcase vent) system adds to it. GM issued a service bulletin to test oil use and replace the pistons and rings. Running low on oil also wears out the timing chain.
issues.next: Check the dipstick at every fill-up and keep the oil full. Ask a dealer to run an oil consumption test and check for bulletin 13-06-01-003. If oil is very low or the oil light comes on, stop driving until it is topped up.

issues.sym: Rattling from the engine at startup, a check engine light with cam timing codes (such as P0016), rough idle, or the engine suddenly quitting and not restarting. A jumped chain can wreck the pistons and valves.
issues.why: The timing chain and its guides on the 2.4L wear and stretch, especially when the engine has been low on oil. Some owners call it a timing belt, but this engine uses a chain.
issues.next: Do not ignore a startup rattle or timing code. Get the chain checked soon; replacing a stretched chain can prevent engine damage.

issues.t: Sudden power loss or stalling with electrical glitches
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving or will not start, and the radio, dash lights or warning lights flicker or cut out. Power steering and power brakes get heavy when the engine stops.
issues.why: Owners have traced many cases to poor battery cable connections, overheated cables or a failing alternator. Some owners were told about bulletins recommending new battery cables.
issues.next: If the engine dies while moving, steer firmly to the roadside and use extra brake pressure. Have the battery cables, grounds and alternator tested before replacing other parts.

issues.t: Key gets stuck in the ignition
issues.sym: The key will not come out after you shift to Park, stays in Accessory, or will not turn off. If you walk away, the battery can drain.
issues.why: The ignition key release is tied to a Park switch in the shifter, and when that switch or its wiring acts up, the car does not know it is in Park.
issues.next: Try moving the shifter firmly into Park again. If it keeps happening, have a shop check the shifter Park switch and ignition lock, and do not leave the car with the key stuck on.

issues.t: Radio and dash cut out when signaling or braking
issues.sym: The radio, dash lights or turn signal sound cut out for a few seconds when you use the turn signal, brake or cruise control.
issues.why: A wiring, ground or battery cable problem lets the voltage dip for a moment.
issues.next: Have the battery cables and grounds checked, since this can be an early sign of the bigger power-loss problem.

issues.t: StabiliTrak, traction and ABS warning lights
issues.sym: The StabiliTrak, traction control, ABS or parking brake warning lights come on, sometimes with reduced engine power.
issues.why: A wheel speed sensor, wiring or low voltage problem can trigger these warnings.
issues.next: The brakes still work normally without ABS, but leave more stopping room. Have the codes read; a wheel speed sensor is a common fix.

issues.sym: The SUV may roll when parked on a slope with the parking brake set.
issues.why: Some 2012 Captiva Sports built from late April to mid-May 2012 have a parking brake that does not meet the holding standard (NHTSA 12V-301).
issues.next: Always shift to Park as well as setting the brake. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer repair it for free.

issues.t: Power steering fluid reservoir can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid under the front, a whining pump, or steering that suddenly gets heavy. Leaking fluid can also land on hot engine parts.
issues.why: The power steering fluid reservoir on some vehicles can leak (NHTSA 11V-591).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer repair it for free. If you smell burning fluid or see smoke, stop and turn the engine off.

issues.sym: The steering suddenly gets very heavy, sometimes along with the engine stalling or warning lights.
issues.why: Loss of assist is often tied to the engine stalling or an electrical fault.
issues.next: Grip the wheel firmly and slow down; you can still steer, just with more effort. Get it inspected before driving again.

issues.t: Charging light on and alternator failure
issues.sym: A battery or charging warning light, dimming lights, the A/C or fan stopping, and eventually a dead battery.
issues.why: The alternator or battery cables can fail and stop keeping the battery charged.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested soon. A car with a failing alternator can stall without much warning.

issues.sym: The airbag light comes on while driving, or the passenger airbag shows OFF with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A fault in the steering wheel clockspring, passenger seat sensor or airbag wiring can set the light.
issues.next: An airbag light means the airbags may not work in a crash. Get the system scanned soon.

issues.t: Transmission slips or will not move
issues.sym: The SUV slips, shifts late, or will not move forward in Drive.
issues.why: Owners have reported failures of the 6-speed automatic.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition, and get it diagnosed before driving far if it slips.

issues.t: Brakes grab or a caliper sticks
issues.sym: The SUV pulls hard or a front brake locks up, a wheel gets very hot, or you smell burning.
issues.why: A front caliper can stick and keep the pads pressed on the rotor.
issues.next: If a wheel smells hot or smokes, pull over and let it cool; do not keep driving. Have the calipers and brake hoses inspected.
